record.title: 1177 B.C.: The Year Civilization Collapsed
record.author: Eric Cline
record.note: Comprehensive scholarly analysis of Late Bronze Age collapse and its causes, relevant to understanding large-scale societal disruption patterns relevant to Quranic narratives about destroyed civilizations.

record.title: Discovering the City of Sodom
record.author: Steven Collins and Latayne C. Scott
record.note: Archaeological investigation of potential Sodom sites in the Dead Sea region, presenting evidence for catastrophic destruction patterns and site identification debates in the southern Levant.

record.title: Babylon: Mesopotamia and the Birth of Civilization
record.author: Paul Kriwaczek
record.note: Historical and archaeological overview of Babylon, including detailed discussion of the Etemenanki ziggurat and multilingual character of the city.

record.title: The Religion of the Nabataeans: A Conspectus
record.author: John F. Healey
record.note: Scholarly examination of Nabatean religious practices and culture in northern Arabia, providing archaeological and epigraphic context for understanding pre-Islamic Arabian societies.

record.title: The Canon of the New Testament: Its Origin, Development, and Significance
record.author: Bruce M. Metzger
record.note: A detailed history of how the twenty-seven-book New Testament canon took shape.

record.title: The Canon of Scripture
record.author: F. F. Bruce
record.note: An evangelical Christian scholar's account of canon formation for both Testaments.

record.title: The Biblical Canon: Its Origin, Transmission, and Authority
record.author: Lee Martin McDonald
record.note: A detailed survey of the debates and criteria behind canon formation.

record.title: The History of the Qur'anic Text from Revelation to Compilation: A Comparative Study with the Old and New Testaments
record.author: Muhammad Mustafa al-Azami
record.note: A Muslim scholar's comparative study of Quranic and biblical transmission.

record.title: The Resurrection of Jesus: History, Experience, Theology
record.author: Gerd Lüdemann
record.note: A historical-critical examination of resurrection and its interpretation in early Christianity; useful for understanding how Christians developed interpretations of Isaiah 53 and other passages.

record.title: Jesus and the Victory of God
record.author: N.T. Wright
record.note: Wright's study of the historical Jesus within first-century Judaism, including Jesus' proclamation, messianic vocation, and movement toward the cross.

record.title: Studies in Jewish Myth and Jewish Messianism
record.author: Yehuda Liebes
record.note: Explores Jewish mystical messianic interpretation; illuminates how Jewish communities engaged creatively with prophetic texts across different periods.

record.title: Essays on Biblical Theology
record.author: Hartmut Gese
record.note: A comparative study of how Jewish and Christian traditions developed distinct hermeneutical methods; foundational for understanding interpretive diversity.

record.title: Jesus in the Qur'an
record.author: Geoffrey Parrinder
record.note: Comparative analysis of Jesus in Christian and Islamic sources, including how different theological frameworks shape accounts of Jesus's final days.

record.title: The Logic of God Incarnate
record.author: Thomas V. Morris
record.note: A rigorous analytic-philosophy defense of the logical coherence of the two-natures doctrine, including the two-minds model discussed in this article.

record.title: Christ in Christian Tradition: From the Apostolic Age to Chalcedon
record.author: Aloys Grillmeier
record.note: The standard scholarly history of how the doctrine of Christ's two natures developed through the early councils, including Nicaea, Ephesus, and Chalcedon.

record.title: The Christian God
record.author: Richard Swinburne
record.note: A leading analytic philosopher of religion's defense of the coherence of the Trinity and Incarnation, useful for readers who want the strongest contemporary philosophical case.

record.title: Al-Jawab al-Sahih li-man Baddala Din al-Masih (The Correct Answer to Those Who Have Corrupted the Religion of Christ)
record.author: Ibn Taymiyyah
record.note: A major classical Muslim theological engagement with Christian doctrines, including the Incarnation and Trinity, argued from within Islamic philosophical categories.

record.title: The Bible, the Qur'an and Science
record.author: Maurice Bucaille
record.note: A well-known early presentation of scientific-scripture comparisons; useful historically, but its claims should be checked against current science and Arabic usage.

record.title: Islam's Quantum Question: Reconciling Muslim Tradition and Modern Science
record.author: Nidhal Guessoum
record.note: A Muslim astrophysicist's critical engagement with modern science, Islamic thought, and scientific-miracle apologetics.

record.title: Tafsir Ibn Kathir (abridged English edition)
record.author: Ibn Kathir (trans. various)
record.note: A widely used classical Sunni commentary that helps distinguish premodern exegesis from later scientific readings.

record.title: Ma'arif-ul-Qur'an
record.author: Mufti Muhammad Shafi (trans. Muhammad Hasan Askari and Muhammad Shamim, rev. Muhammad Taqi Usmani)
record.note: A modern traditional commentary useful for comparing devotional interpretation with scientific-miracle claims.

record.title: On the Reliability of the Old Testament
record.author: Kenneth A. Kitchen
record.note: The fullest recent conservative case, including the argument that Deuteronomy’s covenant form fits second-millennium Hittite treaties rather than seventh-century Assyrian ones.

record.title: Al-Tabari's History of the Prophets and Kings (Tarikh al-Rusul wa'l-Muluk)
record.author: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Jarir al-Tabari
record.note: A foundational Islamic historical work that synthesizes Quranic material, hadith, and historical reports to construct a detailed chronology from creation through the Islamic period; represents traditional Islamic historiography.

record.title: The Bible in History: How Writers Create a Past
record.author: Thomas L. Thompson
record.note: Pimlico paperback, 2000 (first published by Jonathan Cape in 1999; US title The Mythic Past). A critical historical analysis of biblical narrative frameworks; read its reconstruction alongside differing scholarly approaches.

record.title: Narratives of Islamic Origins: The Beginnings of Islamic Historical Writing
record.author: Fred M. Donner
record.note: 1998. An examination of how early Islamic historians constructed their narratives and chronologies, including how Islamic sources related to and reinterpreted biblical and pre-Islamic Arabian materials.

record.title: Battlefields of the Prophet Muhammad: A Contribution to Muslim Military History
record.author: Muhammad Hamidullah
record.note: Historical study computing troop numbers and casualties across the Prophet's military campaigns from classical Arabic sources.

record.title: Did God Really Command Genocide? Coming to Terms with the Justice of God
record.author: Paul Copan and Matthew Flannagan
record.note: Book-length philosophical and theological defense of reading the herem texts as bounded ancient Near Eastern conquest rhetoric (Baker Books, 2014).

record.title: The Lost World of the Israelite Conquest: Covenant, Retribution, and the Fate of the Canaanites
record.author: John H. Walton and J. Harvey Walton
record.note: Argues that herem means removal from ordinary use rather than literal annihilation in every instance, using internal biblical evidence (IVP Academic, 2017).

record.title: Arguing the Just War in Islam
record.author: John Kelsay
record.note: Scholarly study of the shari'a-based jurisprudential tradition on war and its rules protecting non-combatants (Harvard University Press, 2007).

record.title: The Character of Consciousness
record.author: David J. Chalmers
record.note: A major contemporary collection defending the irreducibility of consciousness and developing the hard problem.

record.title: The Study Quran
record.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr and others (editors)
record.note: A translation and extensive commentary useful for tracing classical interpretations of Quranic terms for spirit and self.

record.title: Avicenna's De anima (Arabic Text): Being the Psychological Part of Kitab al-Shifa'
record.author: Fazlur Rahman (editor)
record.note: A primary scholarly edition for Avicenna's influential philosophical psychology; intended for advanced readers.

record.title: Jesus, Interrupted: Revealing the Hidden Contradictions in the Bible
record.author: Bart D. Ehrman
record.note: A readable historical-critical presentation of major tensions in the Bible, best considered alongside scholarly responses and the primary texts.

record.title: The Historical Reliability of the Gospels
record.author: Craig L. Blomberg
record.note: An evangelical defense of Gospel reliability that presents harmonizations of alleged discrepancies.

record.title: The Bible Unearthed
record.author: Israel Finkelstein and Neil Asher Silberman
record.note: A widely discussed archaeological and historical-critical study of biblical narratives; its conclusions remain debated among scholars.

record.title: Islam and Science
record.author: Muzaffar Iqbal
record.note: Historical and philosophical analysis of the relationship between Islamic civilization and scientific inquiry, examining the scriptural foundations and cultural conditions that shaped Islamic scientific tradition.

record.title: Science and Religion in Quest of Truth
record.author: John Polkinghorne
record.note: Theoretical physicist and theologian's careful examination of how science and religious belief address different questions, with analysis of common errors in concordism and the proper relationship between faith and empirical discovery. Yale University Press, 2011.

record.title: The Holy Qur'an and the Sciences of Nature
record.author: Mehdi Golshani
record.note: Iranian physicist-philosopher's exploration of how Quranic teachings relate to natural science, with emphasis on proper interpretation of scriptural language and avoidance of anachronistic readings of ancient texts.

record.title: God's Undertaker: Has Science Buried God?
record.author: John Lennox
record.note: Mathematician and philosopher of science's Christian-apologetics response to New Atheism, examining cosmological fine-tuning, the origin of the universe, and the limits of naturalistic explanation; addressed primarily to a Christian audience, with only passing comparative references to other traditions.

record.title: History of the Christian Church, Vol. 3: Nicene and Post-Nicene Christianity
record.author: Philip Schaff
record.note: A classical historical treatment covering the Council of Nicaea, providing detailed accounts of the proceedings, theological debates, and the biographies of key participants. Valuable for understanding the council from a Christian historical perspective.

record.title: Arius: Heresy and Tradition
record.author: Rowan Williams
record.note: A scholarly examination of Arius and Arianism that challenges some traditional characterizations. Williams presents the theological sophistication of Arian thought and explores why it had significant support in the early church.

record.title: Constantine and the Bishops: The Politics of Intolerance
record.author: H.A. Drake
record.note: Analyzes Constantine's role in church affairs, including his convening of Nicaea. Drake explores how Constantine used religious policy as a tool of imperial governance and the implications for church-state relations.

record.title: The Crucifixion and the Quran: A Study in the History of Muslim Thought
record.author: Todd Lawson
record.note: A scholarly examination of Muslim interpretations of Quran 4:157, from classical exegesis through later Muslim thought.

record.title: Christians, Muslims, and Jesus
record.author: Mona Siddiqui
record.note: A comparative theological study tracing Muslim and Christian views of Jesus from the Quran through medieval polemics to the present, including chapters on early debates over God's oneness and the formation of Christian doctrine—offering an Islamic-informed perspective to balance the largely Christian-historical sources above.

record.title: The Blind Watchmaker: Why the Evidence of Evolution Reveals a Universe Without Design
record.author: Richard Dawkins
record.note: Classic defense of non-teleological evolution and critique of design arguments; influential but polarizing within religious communities.

record.title: Nature Red in Tooth and Claw: Theism and the Problem of Animal Suffering
record.author: Michael J. Murray
record.note: Sophisticated philosophical analysis of how theism relates to evolutionary biology and the theodicy problem of natural suffering, particularly animal pain over evolutionary timescales.

record.title: Evolution and Islam's Quantum Question
record.author: Rana Dajani
record.publisher: Zygon: Journal of Religion and Science
record.note: Published in Zygon: Journal of Religion and Science 47:2 (2012); a contemporary Muslim biologist's perspective on reconciling evolutionary theory with Islamic theology. Zygon: Journal of Religion and Science, vol. 47, no. 2, pp. 343-353, DOI 10.1111/j.1467-9744.2012.01259.x

record.title: Dialogues Concerning Natural Religion
record.author: David Hume
record.note: An eighteenth-century philosophical critique of design arguments that anticipates problems later raised by evolutionary theory.

record.title: The Crusades: A History
record.author: Jonathan Riley-Smith
record.note: Comprehensive historical account examining religious, political, and economic dimensions of the Crusades with attention to multiple perspectives

record.title: The Crusades Through Arab Eyes
record.author: Amin Maalouf
record.note: Provides Islamic and Arab perspective on Crusade-era conflicts, examining how Muslim societies experienced and responded to crusader invasions

record.title: Fighting for the Cross: Crusading to the Holy Land
record.author: Norman Housley
record.note: Examines crusading theology, its development in medieval Christianity, and how religious justifications for warfare were constructed and challenged

record.title: On the Trinity (De Trinitate)
record.author: Augustine of Hippo
record.note: The foundational work of Western Trinitarian theology. Augustine attempts to reconcile biblical passages about God's threeness and oneness through philosophical analysis and seeks human analogies for the Trinity.

record.title: Against the Arians
record.author: Athanasius of Alexandria
record.note: Athanasius's defense of homoousios (consubstantiality) against Arius. These works explain the theological stakes of the Arian controversy and Athanasius's arguments for Christ's full divinity.

record.title: An Exact Exposition of the Orthodox Faith
record.author: John of Damascus
record.note: A systematic presentation of Christian Orthodox doctrine including Trinitarian theology, written in the 8th century. Reflects the Eastern Christian theological tradition shaped by the Councils.

record.title: The Bodies of God and the World of Ancient Israel
record.author: Benjamin D. Sommer
record.note: A scholarly study of theophany and divine presence across the Hebrew Bible, directly addressing the Exodus 33 tension between hearing and seeing God.

record.title: The Gospel According to John I–XII (The Anchor Bible)
record.author: Raymond E. Brown
record.note: A landmark critical commentary on John, with detailed discussion of John 1:18's textual variants and its theology of divine invisibility and revelation in Christ.

record.title: The Study Quran: A New Translation and Commentary
record.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (editor)
record.note: A major contemporary translation and commentary drawing on the classical tafsir tradition, with extended notes on Quran 6:103 and 7:143 and the theology of ru'yat Allah.

record.title: The Formative Period of Islamic Thought
record.author: W. Montgomery Watt
record.note: A scholarly history of early Islamic theological schools, including the Ash'ari–Mu'tazila debate over whether God will be seen in the Hereafter.

record.title: How Jesus Became God: The Exaltation of a Jewish Preacher from Galilee
record.author: Bart D. Ehrman
record.note: A historical-critical account, from a secular New Testament scholar, of how beliefs about Jesus's divine status developed over time.

record.title: Lord Jesus Christ: Devotion to Jesus in Earliest Christianity
record.author: Larry W. Hurtado
record.note: A major academic study tracing how devotion to Jesus developed in the earliest Christian communities.

record.title: An Introduction to New Testament Christology
record.author: Raymond E. Brown
record.note: A careful treatment by a major Catholic scholar, candid about what the New Testament texts do and do not say about Jesus’s divinity.

record.title: Jesus the Jew: A Historian’s Reading of the Gospels
record.author: Geza Vermes
record.note: Reads Jesus within his first-century Jewish context, where titles like ‘son of God’ carried non-divine meanings.

record.title: Christology in the Making
record.author: James D. G. Dunn
record.note: Examines how the doctrine of the incarnation developed within the New Testament period itself.

record.title: Jesus, Prophet of Islam
record.author: Muhammad 'Ata ur-Rahim
record.note: An Islamic perspective on the history of beliefs about Jesus.

record.title: I Am He: The Interpretation of ’Anî Hû’ in Jewish and Early Christian Literature
record.author: Catrin H. Williams
record.note: A specialist study of biblical “I am he” language and its reception in early Christian interpretation.

record.title: The Muslim Jesus: Sayings and Stories in Islamic Literature
record.author: Tarif Khalidi
record.note: Published by Harvard University Press, this collection shows how deeply Jesus is woven into Islamic devotional literature.

record.title: How Jesus Became God
record.author: Bart D. Ehrman
record.note: An academic (non-Muslim, non-confessional) historian's account of how beliefs about Jesus' divinity developed in the earliest centuries.

record.title: Mere Christianity
record.author: C.S. Lewis
record.note: A classic popular presentation of the mainstream Christian case, included so readers can hear that position from one of its best-known advocates.

record.title: The Islamic Jesus: How the King of the Jews Became a Prophet of the Muslims
record.author: Mustafa Akyol
record.note: A Muslim scholar's examination of Jesus' place in Islamic theology and how Islamic and Christian traditions diverge in understanding Jesus' identity and mission, engaging with historical and textual evidence from both scriptures.

record.title: Jesus and the Eyewitnesses: The Gospels as Eyewitness Testimony
record.author: Richard Bauckham
record.note: A Christian New Testament scholar's examination of the Gospel accounts and early Christian belief in Jesus' resurrection and exaltation, relevant to questions of Christological development.

record.title: The Fundamentals of Tawheed (Islamic Monotheism)
record.author: Bilal Philips
record.note: A foundational Islamic text explaining Tawhid as the core principle of Islam, clarifying what constitutes true monotheism and how it differs from polytheism and theological innovations.

record.title: On Christian Theology
record.author: Rowan Williams
record.note: A collection of Christian theological essays, including reflections on Trinity and revelation, divine personhood, and incarnation. Read as a Christian interpretation, not an Islamic authority. ISBN 9780631214403

record.title: Arguing about Gods
record.author: Graham Oppy
record.note: A detailed philosophical critique of major theistic arguments, valuable for testing the case against a sophisticated non-theistic assessment.

record.title: The Existence of God
record.author: Richard Swinburne
record.note: A prominent cumulative-case defense of theism using explanatory reasoning.

record.title: The Quran and the Secular Mind: A Philosophy of Islam
record.author: Shabbir Akhtar
record.note: A philosophical engagement with Quranic claims and modern secular objections.

record.title: The Historical Jesus: A Comprehensive Guide
record.author: Gerd Theissen and Annette Merz
record.note: A comprehensive scholarly overview of Jesus and early Christianity that integrates historical-critical methods with systematic theological reflection. Fortress Press, 1998. Accessible while maintaining academic rigor.

record.title: The Apostolic Fathers: Greek Texts and English Translations
record.author: Michael W. Holmes (translator and editor)
record.note: Authoritative bilingual edition of the Apostolic Fathers (Clement, Ignatius, Polycarp, Didache, and others) with Greek texts and English translations. Baker Academic, 3rd ed., 2007. Primary sources that illuminate early church life, theology, and responses to persecution.

record.title: The Cambridge Ancient History Vol. XI: The High Empire, A.D. 70-192
record.author: Edited by Alan K. Bowman, Peter Garnsey, Dominic Rathbone
record.note: Includes chapters on early Christianity within its broader Roman historical context, balancing Christian sources with external historical evidence.

record.title: An Introduction to the Science of the Hadith (Kitab Ma'rifat Anwa' 'Ilm al-Hadith)
record.author: Ibn al-Salah al-Shahrazuri (13th century), translated by Eerik Dickinson
record.note: A foundational classical work on hadith authentication methodology, part of the Great Books of Islamic Civilization series, explaining jarh wa ta'dil and isnad analysis in detail.

record.title: Studies in Hadith Methodology and Literature
record.author: Muhammad Mustafa al-Azami
record.note: A concise Muslim scholar's account of the classical methods used to grade reports as sound, weak, or fabricated.

record.title: Hadith: Origins and Developments
record.author: Edited by Harald Motzki
record.note: An edited collection of influential scholarly essays (including foundational contributions by Goldziher, Schacht, and Juynboll alongside responses) examining hadith criticism from both classical Islamic and modern Western academic perspectives, with attention to methodological issues in dating and provenance.

record.title: The New Testament Documents: Are They Reliable?
record.author: F. F. Bruce
record.note: A classic evangelical Christian defense of the New Testament's historical reliability, useful as a counterpoint within Christian scholarship itself.

record.title: Hadith: Muhammad's Legacy in the Medieval and Modern World
record.author: Jonathan A. C. Brown
record.note: An accessible academic introduction to how Muslim scholars authenticated reports about the Prophet, including chains of transmission and narrator criticism — the historical ancestor of source-verification systems like this library's.

record.title: The Sanaa Palimpsest: The Transmission of the Qur'an in the First Centuries AH
record.author: Asma Hilali
record.note: An Oxford University Press academic study focused specifically on the Sanaa lower text and its significance.

record.title: Qur'ans of the Umayyads
record.author: François Déroche
record.note: A study by a leading specialist in Quranic codicology on how early Quran manuscripts were physically produced.

record.title: Textual Criticism and Qur'an Manuscripts
record.author: Keith E. Small
record.note: A comparative look at variant readings across early Quran manuscripts.

record.title: Misquoting Jesus
record.author: Bart D. Ehrman
record.note: A widely read introduction to how manuscript variations arose in the Bible's transmission.

record.title: The Developing Human: Clinically Oriented Embryology, with Islamic Additions
record.author: Keith L. Moore, with Abdul Majeed Al-Zindani
record.note: Moore's standard embryology textbook, published in an edition with correlation studies relating its content to Quranic and hadith descriptions; presents the Muslim case for embryological precision in the Quran.

record.title: Medieval Islamic Medicine
record.author: Peter E. Pormann and Emilie Savage-Smith
record.note: Contextualizes Islamic medical knowledge, including theories of human generation, within pre-Islamic and contemporaneous Greco-Roman, Byzantine, and Persian medical traditions, demonstrating continuity rather than unique revelation.

record.title: Langman's Medical Embryology
record.author: T.W. Sadler
record.note: Standard modern embryology textbook providing detailed, stage-by-stage developmental biology from fertilization through birth.

record.title: The Genesis of Science: How the Christian Middle Ages Launched the Scientific Revolution
record.author: James Hannam
record.note: Explores how Christian theologians engaged with natural philosophy and science, contextualizing the relationship between scripture and scientific inquiry historically.

record.title: Christ in Islam and Christianity: The Representation of Jesus in the Qur'an and the Classical Muslim Commentaries
record.author: Neal Robinson
record.publisher: State University of New York Press
record.note: Academic study of Quranic and classical Muslim interpretations of Jesus, including his return, crucifixion, miracles, and birth. ISBN 9780791405581

record.title: Eve and Adam: Jewish, Christian, and Muslim Readings on Genesis and Gender
record.author: Kristen E. Kvam, Linda S. Schearing, and Valarie H. Ziegler (eds.)
record.note: An anthology of primary sources from all three traditions on Eve and the fall, providing a side-by-side history of interpretation (Indiana University Press, 1999).

record.title: Women in the Qur'an, Traditions, and Interpretation
record.author: Barbara Freyer Stowasser
record.note: Scholarly analysis of Quranic passages concerning women, including inheritance and testimony, examining both classical and modern interpretations.

record.title: Adam, Eve, and the Serpent
record.author: Elaine Pagels
record.note: A historian’s account of how early Christians, from Paul to Augustine, transformed the Genesis story and built doctrines of sin and sexuality on it (Random House, 1988).

record.title: God and the Rhetoric of Sexuality
record.author: Phyllis Trible
record.note: A close literary reading of Genesis 2-3 arguing that the text describes rather than prescribes male rule; influential in modern Christian exegesis of Genesis 3:16 (Fortress Press, 1978).

record.title: Qur'an and Woman: Rereading the Sacred Text from a Woman's Perspective
record.author: Amina Wadud
record.note: Foundational work examining Quranic perspectives on women and reinterpreting Islamic theological principles through a feminist lens, demonstrating women's agency in Quranic narrative.

record.title: Great Women of Islam: Who Were Given the Good News of Paradise
record.author: Mahmood Ahmad Ghadanfar (reviewed by Safi-ur-Rahman al-Mubarakpuri)
record.note: Biographical collection of female companions including detailed accounts of their scholarly contributions, leadership roles, and legal authority during the Prophet's lifetime and early Islamic period.

record.title: Believing Women in Islam: Unreading Patriarchal Interpretations of the Qur'an
record.author: Asma Barlas
record.note: Critical examination of how patriarchal interpretations have shaped Quranic readings, with detailed exploration of Quranic support for women's agency and equality within Islamic theology.

record.title: Hildegard of Bingen: The Woman of Her Age
record.author: Fiona Maddocks
record.note: Biographical study of a major medieval Christian theologian and mystic, illustrating the substantial intellectual contributions of women to Christian theology and the institutional support for female scholarly authority in medieval Christendom.

record.title: Islam: A Very Short Introduction
record.author: Malise Ruthven
record.note: An accessible overview of Islamic belief and history published by Oxford University Press.

record.title: Al-Ghazali on Invocations and Supplications
record.author: Abu Hamid al-Ghazali; translated by Kojiro Nakamura
record.note: A practical and spiritual treatment of remembrance and personal prayer, published by The Islamic Texts Society.

record.title: Cur Deus Homo (Why God Became Man)
record.author: Anselm of Canterbury
record.note: The medieval work that established the satisfaction theory of atonement, the classical Christian answer to why Christ's death was necessary for sin.

record.title: Christus Victor
record.author: Gustaf Aulén
record.note: An influential historical survey of the main Christian atonement models — ransom/victory, satisfaction, and moral influence — showing that Christianity has held several understandings of the cross.

record.title: The Cross of Christ
record.author: John Stott
record.note: A widely respected modern evangelical defense of penal substitution; recommended so readers can hear the mainstream Protestant case argued by one of its ablest advocates.

record.title: On Repentance (Kitab al-Tawba, from Ihya Ulum al-Din)
record.author: Abu Hamid al-Ghazali
record.note: The celebrated Muslim theologian’s treatment of tawbah: its conditions, its psychology, and the vastness of divine mercy.

record.title: Christianity and Rabbinic Judaism: A Parallel History of Their Origins and Early Development
record.author: Hershel Shanks (ed.)
record.note: Edited volume contextualizing Jewish genealogical practices and expectations regarding Messianic descent; includes a chapter by James H. Charlesworth, "Christians and Jews in the First Six Centuries."

record.title: The Birth of the Messiah: A Commentary on the Infancy Narratives in the Gospels of Matthew and Luke
record.author: Raymond E. Brown
record.note: Comprehensive scholarly treatment of Matthew and Luke's genealogies, sources, and theological purposes.

record.title: The Purpose of the Biblical Genealogies: With Special Reference to the Setting of the Genealogies of Jesus
record.author: Marshall D. Johnson
record.note: A dedicated academic monograph analyzing the form and function of biblical genealogies, with a major focus on reconciling and interpreting Matthew's and Luke's genealogies of Jesus.

record.title: Al-Tawhid: Its Implications for Thought and Life
record.author: Ismail Raji al-Faruqi
record.note: Examines the Islamic concept of tawhid across philosophy, ethics, and comparative religion, including its contrast with Christian and Western theological frameworks.

record.title: Summa Theologiae, Prima Pars, Questions 3-14
record.author: Thomas Aquinas
record.note: Classical Christian discussion of divine simplicity, perfection, goodness, infinity, immutability, eternity, unity, and knowledge. Divine power is treated separately in Prima Pars, Question 25.

record.title: Knowing the Unknowable God: Ibn-Sina, Maimonides, Aquinas
record.author: David Burrell
record.note: Comparative analysis of how Islamic and Christian theology understand God's attributes and the limits of human knowledge of the divine.

record.title: God, Evil and the Limits of Theology
record.author: Karen Kilby
record.note: Contemporary Christian theological work examining divine nature, theodicy, and the doctrine of the Trinity.

record.title: Jesus, Interrupted: Revealing the Hidden Contradictions in the Bible (And Why We Don't Know About Them)
record.author: Bart D. Ehrman
record.note: A widely read overview of mainstream scholarly conclusions on Gospel authorship, dating, and the Synoptic Problem.

record.title: An Introduction to the New Testament
record.author: Raymond E. Brown
record.note: A standard Catholic scholarly textbook surveying authorship and dating debates for each New Testament book.

record.title: The Historical Figure of Jesus
record.author: E. P. Sanders
record.note: A widely used introduction to historical study of Jesus and the early Christian movement.

record.title: Hadith Literature: Its Origin, Development and Special Features
record.author: M. Zubayr Siddiqi
record.note: A classic account of the science of hadith transmission and chain evaluation.

record.title: The Reformation: A Very Short Introduction
record.author: Peter Marshall
record.note: Comprehensive examination of the Reformation and Martin Luther's theological innovations, including the doctrine of sola fide and its historical context.

record.title: Justification: God's Plan and Paul's Vision
record.author: N.T. Wright
record.note: Modern scholarly investigation of Paul's doctrine of justification, in which N.T. Wright defends his 'New Perspective on Paul' reading against Reformed critics (principally John Piper) — an intra-Protestant debate over how justification and covenant membership relate.

record.title: The Orthodox Church
record.author: Timothy Ware
record.note: Introduction to Orthodox Christian theology and practice, including their understanding of grace, deification, and the synergistic relationship between divine and human action.

record.title: Fundamentals of Islamic Thought: God, Man and the Universe
record.author: Murtaza Mutahhari
record.note: Systematic exploration of core Islamic theological concepts, including the relationship between faith, action, and God's will, with special attention to human responsibility within divine sovereignty.

record.title: The Idea of the Holy: An Inquiry into the Non-Rational Factor in the Idea of the Divine
record.author: Rudolf Otto
record.note: Explores how both Western and Eastern religions attempt to describe the transcendent through human language and experience.

record.title: The Problem of Pain
record.author: C.S. Lewis
record.note: A Christian theological treatment of suffering and hell that grapples with how to understand divine justice and eternal consequences.

record.title: What Is Islam? The Importance of Being Islamic
record.author: Shahab Ahmed
record.note: A scholarly investigation into how Islam as a comprehensive worldview encompasses theological doctrine, ethics, and metaphysics—providing context for understanding Islamic theological debates on eschatology and divine justice.

record.title: Surprised by Hope: Rethinking Heaven, the Resurrection, and the Mission of the Church
record.author: N.T. Wright
record.note: A Christian account of hope in bodily resurrection and renewed creation, distinguished from the idea that final salvation is escape from the world into heaven.

record.title: FAQ: Rules of War
record.author: International Committee of the Red Cross
record.note: A public introduction to civilian protection and prohibited conduct under international humanitarian law; it explains legal rules, not every disputed fact in a specific incident.

record.title: Under Crescent and Cross: The Jews in the Middle Ages

record.title: Science and Religion: A Very Short Introduction

record.title: Oceanography: An Illustrated Text

record.title: The Qur'anic Phenomenon: An Essay of a Theory on the Qur'an
record.author: Malek Bennabi
record.note: Islamic scholar's examination of Quranic structure and content as evidence of divine revelation.

record.title: Geography of Strabo
record.author: Strabo (trans. H. C. Hamilton and W. Falconer)

record.title: The Lawful and the Prohibited in Islam (Al-Halal wa-Al-Haram fi-Al-Islam)

record.title: Shari'ah Law: An Introduction

record.title: The Resurrection of Jesus: A New Historiographical Approach

record.title: The Oxford Handbook of Eschatology

record.translation: So We saved him and those with him by mercy from Us. And We eliminated those who denied Our signs, and they were not [at all] believers.
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: وَإِلَىٰ ثَمُودَ أَخَاهُمْ صَٰلِحًۭا ۗ قَالَ يَٰقَوْمِ ٱعْبُدُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ مَا لَكُم مِّنْ إِلَٰهٍ غَيْرُهُۥ ۖ قَدْ جَآءَتْكُم بَيِّنَةٌۭ مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ ۖ هَٰذِهِۦ نَاقَةُ ٱللَّهِ لَكُمْ ءَايَةًۭ ۖ فَذَرُوهَا تَأْكُلْ فِىٓ أَرْضِ ٱللَّهِ ۖ وَلَا تَمَسُّوهَا بِسُوٓءٍۢ فَيَأْخُذَكُمْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌۭ
record.translation: And to the Thamud [We sent] their brother Salih. He said, "O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him. There has come to you clear evidence from your Lord. This is the she-camel of Allah [sent] to you as a sign. So leave her to eat within Allah 's land and do not touch her with harm, lest there seize you a painful punishment.
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: فَأَخَذَتْهُمُ ٱلرَّجْفَةُ فَأَصْبَحُوا۟ فِى دَارِهِمْ جَٰثِمِينَ
record.translation: So the earthquake seized them, and they became within their home [corpses] fallen prone.
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: وَلُوطًا إِذْ قَالَ لِقَوْمِهِۦٓ أَتَأْتُونَ ٱلْفَٰحِشَةَ مَا سَبَقَكُم بِهَا مِنْ أَحَدٍۢ مِّنَ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
record.translation: And [We had sent] Lot when he said to his people, "Do you commit such immorality as no one has preceded you with from among the worlds?
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: وَأَمْطَرْنَا عَلَيْهِم مَّطَرًۭا ۖ فَٱنظُرْ كَيْفَ كَانَ عَٰقِبَةُ ٱلْمُجْرِمِينَ
record.translation: And We rained upon them a rain [of stones]. Then see how was the end of the criminals.
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: كَذَّبَتْ عَادٌ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ
record.translation: 'Aad denied the messengers
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: كَذَّبَتْ ثَمُودُ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ
record.translation: Thamud denied the messengers
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: فَأَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَىٰ مُوسَىٰٓ أَنِ ٱضْرِب بِّعَصَاكَ ٱلْبَحْرَ ۖ فَٱنفَلَقَ فَكَانَ كُلُّ فِرْقٍۢ كَٱلطَّوْدِ ٱلْعَظِيمِ
record.translation: Then We inspired to Moses, "Strike with your staff the sea," and it parted, and each portion was like a great towering mountain.
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: أَتَأْتُونَ ٱلذُّكْرَانَ مِنَ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
record.translation: Do you approach males among the worlds
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: فَأَتْبَعَهُمْ فِرْعَوْنُ بِجُنُودِهِۦ فَغَشِيَهُم مِّنَ ٱلْيَمِّ مَا غَشِيَهُمْ
record.translation: So Pharaoh pursued them with his soldiers, and there covered them from the sea that which covered them,
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: وَلُوطًا إِذْ قَالَ لِقَوْمِهِۦٓ إِنَّكُمْ لَتَأْتُونَ ٱلْفَٰحِشَةَ مَا سَبَقَكُم بِهَا مِنْ أَحَدٍۢ مِّنَ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
record.translation: And [mention] Lot, when he said to his people, "Indeed, you commit such immorality as no one has preceded you with from among the worlds.
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: وَقَالَ فِرْعَوْنُ يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلْمَلَأُ مَا عَلِمْتُ لَكُم مِّنْ إِلَٰهٍ غَيْرِى فَأَوْقِدْ لِى يَٰهَٰمَٰنُ عَلَى ٱلطِّينِ فَٱجْعَل لِّى صَرْحًۭا لَّعَلِّىٓ أَطَّلِعُ إِلَىٰٓ إِلَٰهِ مُوسَىٰ وَإِنِّى لَأَظُنُّهُۥ مِنَ ٱلْكَٰذِبِينَ
record.translation: And Pharaoh said, "O eminent ones, I have not known you to have a god other than me. Then ignite for me, O Haman, [a fire] upon the clay and make for me a tower that I may look at the God of Moses. And indeed, I do think he is among the liars."
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: وَٱتْرُكِ ٱلْبَحْرَ رَهْوًا ۖ إِنَّهُمْ جُندٌۭ مُّغْرَقُونَ
record.translation: And leave the sea in stillness. Indeed, they are an army to be drowned."
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: أَلَمْ تَرَ كَيْفَ فَعَلَ رَبُّكَ بِعَادٍ
record.translation: Have you not considered how your Lord dealt with 'Aad -
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: كَذَّبَتْ ثَمُودُ بِطَغْوَىٰهَآ
record.translation: Thamud denied [their prophet] by reason of their transgression,
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: وَٱتَّبَعُوا۟ مَا تَتْلُوا۟ ٱلشَّيَٰطِينُ عَلَىٰ مُلْكِ سُلَيْمَٰنَ ۖ وَمَا كَفَرَ سُلَيْمَٰنُ وَلَٰكِنَّ ٱلشَّيَٰطِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ يُعَلِّمُونَ ٱلنَّاسَ ٱلسِّحْرَ وَمَآ أُنزِلَ عَلَى ٱلْمَلَكَيْنِ بِبَابِلَ هَٰرُوتَ وَمَٰرُوتَ ۚ وَمَا يُعَلِّمَانِ مِنْ أَحَدٍ حَتَّىٰ يَقُولَآ إِنَّمَا نَحْنُ فِتْنَةٌۭ فَلَا تَكْفُرْ ۖ فَيَتَعَلَّمُونَ مِنْهُمَا مَا يُفَرِّقُونَ بِهِۦ بَيْنَ ٱلْمَرْءِ وَزَوْجِهِۦ ۚ وَمَا هُم بِضَآرِّينَ بِهِۦ مِنْ أَحَدٍ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِ ٱللَّهِ ۚ وَيَتَعَلَّمُونَ مَا يَضُرُّهُمْ وَلَا يَنفَعُهُمْ ۚ وَلَقَدْ عَلِمُوا۟ لَمَنِ ٱشْتَرَىٰهُ مَا لَهُۥ فِى ٱلْءَاخِرَةِ مِنْ خَلَٰقٍۢ ۚ وَلَبِئْسَ مَا شَرَوْا۟ بِهِۦٓ أَنفُسَهُمْ ۚ لَوْ كَانُوا۟ يَعْلَمُونَ
record.translation: And they followed [instead] what the devils had recited during the reign of Solomon. It was not Solomon who disbelieved, but the devils disbelieved, teaching people magic and that which was revealed to the two angels at Babylon, Harut and Marut. But the two angels do not teach anyone unless they say, "We are a trial, so do not disbelieve [by practicing magic]." And [yet] they learn from them that by which they cause separation between a man and his wife. But they do not harm anyone through it except by permission of Allah. And the people learn what harms them and does not benefit them. But the Children of Israel certainly knew that whoever purchased the magic would not have in the Hereafter any share. And wretched is that for which they sold themselves, if they only knew.
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: وَقَالَ فِرْعَوْنُ يَٰهَٰمَٰنُ ٱبْنِ لِى صَرْحًۭا لَّعَلِّىٓ أَبْلُغُ ٱلْأَسْبَٰبَ
record.translation: And Pharaoh said, "O Haman, construct for me a tower that I might reach the ways -
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: حُرِّمَتْ عَلَيْكُمُ ٱلْمَيْتَةُ وَٱلدَّمُ وَلَحْمُ ٱلْخِنزِيرِ وَمَآ أُهِلَّ لِغَيْرِ ٱللَّهِ بِهِۦ وَٱلْمُنْخَنِقَةُ وَٱلْمَوْقُوذَةُ وَٱلْمُتَرَدِّيَةُ وَٱلنَّطِيحَةُ وَمَآ أَكَلَ ٱلسَّبُعُ إِلَّا مَا ذَكَّيْتُمْ وَمَا ذُبِحَ عَلَى ٱلنُّصُبِ وَأَن تَسْتَقْسِمُوا۟ بِٱلْأَزْلَٰمِ ۚ ذَٰلِكُمْ فِسْقٌ ۗ ٱلْيَوْمَ يَئِسَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ مِن دِينِكُمْ فَلَا تَخْشَوْهُمْ وَٱخْشَوْنِ ۚ ٱلْيَوْمَ أَكْمَلْتُ لَكُمْ دِينَكُمْ وَأَتْمَمْتُ عَلَيْكُمْ نِعْمَتِى وَرَضِيتُ لَكُمُ ٱلْإِسْلَٰمَ دِينًۭا ۚ فَمَنِ ٱضْطُرَّ فِى مَخْمَصَةٍ غَيْرَ مُتَجَانِفٍۢ لِّإِثْمٍۢ ۙ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورٌۭ رَّحِيمٌۭ
record.translation: Prohibited to you are dead animals, blood, the flesh of swine, and that which has been dedicated to other than Allah, and [those animals] killed by strangling or by a violent blow or by a head-long fall or by the goring of horns, and those from which a wild animal has eaten, except what you [are able to] slaughter [before its death], and those which are sacrificed on stone altars, and [prohibited is] that you seek decision through divining arrows. That is grave disobedience. This day those who disbelieve have despaired of [defeating] your religion; so fear them not, but fear Me. This day I have perfected for you your religion and completed My favor upon you and have approved for you Islam as religion. But whoever is forced by severe hunger with no inclination to sin - then indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: إِنَّا نَحْنُ نَزَّلْنَا ٱلذِّكْرَ وَإِنَّا لَهُۥ لَحَٰفِظُونَ
record.translation: Indeed, it is We who sent down the Qur'an and indeed, We will be its guardian.
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: إِذْ قَالَتِ ٱلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةُ يَٰمَرْيَمُ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُبَشِّرُكِ بِكَلِمَةٍۢ مِّنْهُ ٱسْمُهُ ٱلْمَسِيحُ عِيسَى ٱبْنُ مَرْيَمَ وَجِيهًۭا فِى ٱلدُّنْيَا وَٱلْءَاخِرَةِ وَمِنَ ٱلْمُقَرَّبِينَ
record.translation: [And mention] when the angels said, "O Mary, indeed Allah gives you good tidings of a word from Him, whose name will be the Messiah, Jesus, the son of Mary - distinguished in this world and the Hereafter and among those brought near [to Allah].
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: يَٰٓأَهْلَ ٱلْكِتَٰبِ لَا تَغْلُوا۟ فِى دِينِكُمْ وَلَا تَقُولُوا۟ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ إِلَّا ٱلْحَقَّ ۚ إِنَّمَا ٱلْمَسِيحُ عِيسَى ٱبْنُ مَرْيَمَ رَسُولُ ٱللَّهِ وَكَلِمَتُهُۥٓ أَلْقَىٰهَآ إِلَىٰ مَرْيَمَ وَرُوحٌۭ مِّنْهُ ۖ فَـَٔامِنُوا۟ بِٱللَّهِ وَرُسُلِهِۦ ۖ وَلَا تَقُولُوا۟ ثَلَٰثَةٌ ۚ ٱنتَهُوا۟ خَيْرًۭا لَّكُمْ ۚ إِنَّمَا ٱللَّهُ إِلَٰهٌۭ وَٰحِدٌۭ ۖ سُبْحَٰنَهُۥٓ أَن يَكُونَ لَهُۥ وَلَدٌۭ ۘ لَّهُۥ مَا فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ ۗ وَكَفَىٰ بِٱللَّهِ وَكِيلًۭا
record.translation: O People of the Scripture, do not commit excess in your religion or say about Allah except the truth. The Messiah, Jesus, the son of Mary, was but a messenger of Allah and His word which He directed to Mary and a soul [created at a command] from Him. So believe in Allah and His messengers. And do not say, "Three"; desist - it is better for you. Indeed, Allah is but one God. Exalted is He above having a son. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs.
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: وَإِذْ قَالَ عِيسَى ٱبْنُ مَرْيَمَ يَٰبَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ إِنِّى رَسُولُ ٱللَّهِ إِلَيْكُم مُّصَدِّقًۭا لِّمَا بَيْنَ يَدَىَّ مِنَ ٱلتَّوْرَىٰةِ وَمُبَشِّرًۢا بِرَسُولٍۢ يَأْتِى مِنۢ بَعْدِى ٱسْمُهُۥٓ أَحْمَدُ ۖ فَلَمَّا جَآءَهُم بِٱلْبَيِّنَٰتِ قَالُوا۟ هَٰذَا سِحْرٌۭ مُّبِينٌۭ
record.translation: And [mention] when Jesus, the son of Mary, said, "O children of Israel, indeed I am the messenger of Allah to you confirming what came before me of the Torah and bringing good tidings of a messenger to come after me, whose name is Ahmad." But when he came to them with clear evidences, they said, "This is obvious magic."
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: وَأَنزَلْنَآ إِلَيْكَ ٱلْكِتَٰبَ بِٱلْحَقِّ مُصَدِّقًۭا لِّمَا بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ مِنَ ٱلْكِتَٰبِ وَمُهَيْمِنًا عَلَيْهِ ۖ فَٱحْكُم بَيْنَهُم بِمَآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ ۖ وَلَا تَتَّبِعْ أَهْوَآءَهُمْ عَمَّا جَآءَكَ مِنَ ٱلْحَقِّ ۚ لِكُلٍّۢ جَعَلْنَا مِنكُمْ شِرْعَةًۭ وَمِنْهَاجًۭا ۚ وَلَوْ شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ لَجَعَلَكُمْ أُمَّةًۭ وَٰحِدَةًۭ وَلَٰكِن لِّيَبْلُوَكُمْ فِى مَآ ءَاتَىٰكُمْ ۖ فَٱسْتَبِقُوا۟ ٱلْخَيْرَٰتِ ۚ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ مَرْجِعُكُمْ جَمِيعًۭا فَيُنَبِّئُكُم بِمَا كُنتُمْ فِيهِ تَخْتَلِفُونَ
record.translation: And We have revealed to you, [O Muhammad], the Book in truth, confirming that which preceded it of the Scripture and as a criterion over it. So judge between them by what Allah has revealed and do not follow their inclinations away from what has come to you of the truth. To each of you We prescribed a law and a method. Had Allah willed, He would have made you one nation [united in religion], but [He intended] to test you in what He has given you; so race to [all that is] good. To Allah is your return all together, and He will [then] inform you concerning that over which you used to differ.
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: قُلْ أَغَيْرَ ٱللَّهِ أَبْغِى رَبًّۭا وَهُوَ رَبُّ كُلِّ شَىْءٍۢ ۚ وَلَا تَكْسِبُ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ إِلَّا عَلَيْهَا ۚ وَلَا تَزِرُ وَازِرَةٌۭ وِزْرَ أُخْرَىٰ ۚ ثُمَّ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكُم مَّرْجِعُكُمْ فَيُنَبِّئُكُم بِمَا كُنتُمْ فِيهِ تَخْتَلِفُونَ
record.translation: Say, "Is it other than Allah I should desire as a lord while He is the Lord of all things? And every soul earns not [blame] except against itself, and no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another. Then to your Lord is your return, and He will inform you concerning that over which you used to differ."
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: وَقَوْلِهِمْ إِنَّا قَتَلْنَا ٱلْمَسِيحَ عِيسَى ٱبْنَ مَرْيَمَ رَسُولَ ٱللَّهِ وَمَا قَتَلُوهُ وَمَا صَلَبُوهُ وَلَٰكِن شُبِّهَ لَهُمْ ۚ وَإِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱخْتَلَفُوا۟ فِيهِ لَفِى شَكٍّۢ مِّنْهُ ۚ مَا لَهُم بِهِۦ مِنْ عِلْمٍ إِلَّا ٱتِّبَاعَ ٱلظَّنِّ ۚ وَمَا قَتَلُوهُ يَقِينًۢا
record.translation: And [for] their saying, "Indeed, we have killed the Messiah, Jesus, the son of Mary, the messenger of Allah." And they did not kill him, nor did they crucify him; but [another] was made to resemble him to them. And indeed, those who differ over it are in doubt about it. They have no knowledge of it except the following of assumption. And they did not kill him, for certain.
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: بَل رَّفَعَهُ ٱللَّهُ إِلَيْهِ ۚ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ عَزِيزًا حَكِيمًۭا
record.translation: Rather, Allah raised him to Himself. And ever is Allah Exalted in Might and Wise.
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: لَمْ يَلِدْ وَلَمْ يُولَدْ
record.translation: He neither begets nor is born,
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: مَا كَانَ لِلَّهِ أَن يَتَّخِذَ مِن وَلَدٍۢ ۖ سُبْحَٰنَهُۥٓ ۚ إِذَا قَضَىٰٓ أَمْرًۭا فَإِنَّمَا يَقُولُ لَهُۥ كُن فَيَكُونُ
record.translation: It is not [befitting] for Allah to take a son; exalted is He! When He decrees an affair, He only says to it, "Be," and it is.
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: ذَٰلِكَ عِيسَى ٱبْنُ مَرْيَمَ ۚ قَوْلَ ٱلْحَقِّ ٱلَّذِى فِيهِ يَمْتَرُونَ
record.translation: That is Jesus, the son of Mary - the word of truth about which they are in dispute.
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: لَا ٱلشَّمْسُ يَنۢبَغِى لَهَآ أَن تُدْرِكَ ٱلْقَمَرَ وَلَا ٱلَّيْلُ سَابِقُ ٱلنَّهَارِ ۚ وَكُلٌّۭ فِى فَلَكٍۢ يَسْبَحُونَ
record.translation: It is not allowable for the sun to reach the moon, nor does the night overtake the day, but each, in an orbit, is swimming.
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَ ٱلَّيْلَ وَٱلنَّهَارَ وَٱلشَّمْسَ وَٱلْقَمَرَ ۖ كُلٌّۭ فِى فَلَكٍۢ يَسْبَحُونَ
record.translation: And it is He who created the night and the day and the sun and the moon; all [heavenly bodies] in an orbit are swimming.
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: ۞ فَلَآ أُقْسِمُ بِمَوَٰقِعِ ٱلنُّجُومِ
record.translation: Then I swear by the setting of the stars,
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: وَإِنَّهُۥ لَقَسَمٌۭ لَّوْ تَعْلَمُونَ عَظِيمٌ
record.translation: And indeed, it is an oath - if you could know - [most] great.
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: إِنَّهُۥ لَقُرْءَانٌۭ كَرِيمٌۭ
record.translation: Indeed, it is a noble Qur'an
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: فِى كِتَٰبٍۢ مَّكْنُونٍۢ
record.translation: In a Register well-protected;
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: وَتَرَى ٱلْجِبَالَ تَحْسَبُهَا جَامِدَةًۭ وَهِىَ تَمُرُّ مَرَّ ٱلسَّحَابِ ۚ صُنْعَ ٱللَّهِ ٱلَّذِىٓ أَتْقَنَ كُلَّ شَىْءٍ ۚ إِنَّهُۥ خَبِيرٌۢ بِمَا تَفْعَلُونَ
record.translation: And you see the mountains, thinking them rigid, while they will pass as the passing of clouds. [It is] the work of Allah, who perfected all things. Indeed, He is Acquainted with that which you do.
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِى مَدَّ ٱلْأَرْضَ وَجَعَلَ فِيهَا رَوَٰسِىَ وَأَنْهَٰرًۭا ۖ وَمِن كُلِّ ٱلثَّمَرَٰتِ جَعَلَ فِيهَا زَوْجَيْنِ ٱثْنَيْنِ ۖ يُغْشِى ٱلَّيْلَ ٱلنَّهَارَ ۚ إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَءَايَٰتٍۢ لِّقَوْمٍۢ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ
record.translation: And it is He who spread the earth and placed therein firmly set mountains and rivers; and from all of the fruits He made therein two mates; He causes the night to cover the day. Indeed in that are signs for a people who give thought.
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: سُبْحَٰنَ ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَ ٱلْأَزْوَٰجَ كُلَّهَا مِمَّا تُنۢبِتُ ٱلْأَرْضُ وَمِنْ أَنفُسِهِمْ وَمِمَّا لَا يَعْلَمُونَ
record.translation: Exalted is He who created all pairs - from what the earth grows and from themselves and from that which they do not know.
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: أَوَلَمْ يَرَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوٓا۟ أَنَّ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضَ كَانَتَا رَتْقًۭا فَفَتَقْنَٰهُمَا ۖ وَجَعَلْنَا مِنَ ٱلْمَآءِ كُلَّ شَىْءٍ حَىٍّ ۖ أَفَلَا يُؤْمِنُونَ
record.translation: Have those who disbelieved not considered that the heavens and the earth were a joined entity, and We separated them and made from water every living thing? Then will they not believe?
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: لَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنَا رُسُلَنَا بِٱلْبَيِّنَٰتِ وَأَنزَلْنَا مَعَهُمُ ٱلْكِتَٰبَ وَٱلْمِيزَانَ لِيَقُومَ ٱلنَّاسُ بِٱلْقِسْطِ ۖ وَأَنزَلْنَا ٱلْحَدِيدَ فِيهِ بَأْسٌۭ شَدِيدٌۭ وَمَنَٰفِعُ لِلنَّاسِ وَلِيَعْلَمَ ٱللَّهُ مَن يَنصُرُهُۥ وَرُسُلَهُۥ بِٱلْغَيْبِ ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ قَوِىٌّ عَزِيزٌۭ
record.translation: We have already sent Our messengers with clear evidences and sent down with them the Scripture and the balance that the people may maintain [their affairs] in justice. And We sent down iron, wherein is great military might and benefits for the people, and so that Allah may make evident those who support Him and His messengers unseen. Indeed, Allah is Powerful and Exalted in Might.
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: خَلَقَكُم مِّن نَّفْسٍۢ وَٰحِدَةٍۢ ثُمَّ جَعَلَ مِنْهَا زَوْجَهَا وَأَنزَلَ لَكُم مِّنَ ٱلْأَنْعَٰمِ ثَمَٰنِيَةَ أَزْوَٰجٍۢ ۚ يَخْلُقُكُمْ فِى بُطُونِ أُمَّهَٰتِكُمْ خَلْقًۭا مِّنۢ بَعْدِ خَلْقٍۢ فِى ظُلُمَٰتٍۢ ثَلَٰثٍۢ ۚ ذَٰلِكُمُ ٱللَّهُ رَبُّكُمْ لَهُ ٱلْمُلْكُ ۖ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ ۖ فَأَنَّىٰ تُصْرَفُونَ
record.translation: He created you from one soul. Then He made from it its mate, and He produced for you from the grazing livestock eight mates. He creates you in the wombs of your mothers, creation after creation, within three darknesses. That is Allah, your Lord; to Him belongs dominion. There is no deity except Him, so how are you averted?
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: يَٰبَنِىٓ ءَادَمَ قَدْ أَنزَلْنَا عَلَيْكُمْ لِبَاسًۭا يُوَٰرِى سَوْءَٰتِكُمْ وَرِيشًۭا ۖ وَلِبَاسُ ٱلتَّقْوَىٰ ذَٰلِكَ خَيْرٌۭ ۚ ذَٰلِكَ مِنْ ءَايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَذَّكَّرُونَ
record.translation: O children of Adam, We have bestowed upon you clothing to conceal your private parts and as adornment. But the clothing of righteousness - that is best. That is from the signs of Allah that perhaps they will remember.
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: تَبَارَكَ ٱلَّذِى جَعَلَ فِى ٱلسَّمَآءِ بُرُوجًۭا وَجَعَلَ فِيهَا سِرَٰجًۭا وَقَمَرًۭا مُّنِيرًۭا
record.translation: Blessed is He who has placed in the sky great stars and placed therein a [burning] lamp and luminous moon.
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: وَجَعَلَ ٱلْقَمَرَ فِيهِنَّ نُورًۭا وَجَعَلَ ٱلشَّمْسَ سِرَاجًۭا
record.translation: And made the moon therein a [reflected] light and made the sun a burning lamp?
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: هُوَ ٱلَّذِى جَعَلَ ٱلشَّمْسَ ضِيَآءًۭ وَٱلْقَمَرَ نُورًۭا وَقَدَّرَهُۥ مَنَازِلَ لِتَعْلَمُوا۟ عَدَدَ ٱلسِّنِينَ وَٱلْحِسَابَ ۚ مَا خَلَقَ ٱللَّهُ ذَٰلِكَ إِلَّا بِٱلْحَقِّ ۚ يُفَصِّلُ ٱلْءَايَٰتِ لِقَوْمٍۢ يَعْلَمُونَ
record.translation: It is He who made the sun a shining light and the moon a derived light and determined for it phases - that you may know the number of years and account [of time]. Allah has not created this except in truth. He details the signs for a people who know
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: وَإِذْ قَالَ إِبْرَٰهِۦمُ رَبِّ أَرِنِى كَيْفَ تُحْىِ ٱلْمَوْتَىٰ ۖ قَالَ أَوَلَمْ تُؤْمِن ۖ قَالَ بَلَىٰ وَلَٰكِن لِّيَطْمَئِنَّ قَلْبِى ۖ قَالَ فَخُذْ أَرْبَعَةًۭ مِّنَ ٱلطَّيْرِ فَصُرْهُنَّ إِلَيْكَ ثُمَّ ٱجْعَلْ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ جَبَلٍۢ مِّنْهُنَّ جُزْءًۭا ثُمَّ ٱدْعُهُنَّ يَأْتِينَكَ سَعْيًۭا ۚ وَٱعْلَمْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌۭ
record.translation: And [mention] when Abraham said, "My Lord, show me how You give life to the dead." [Allah] said, "Have you not believed?" He said, "Yes, but [I ask] only that my heart may be satisfied." [Allah] said, "Take four birds and commit them to yourself. Then [after slaughtering them] put on each hill a portion of them; then call them - they will come [flying] to you in haste. And know that Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise."
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: ۞ إِنَّ قَٰرُونَ كَانَ مِن قَوْمِ مُوسَىٰ فَبَغَىٰ عَلَيْهِمْ ۖ وَءَاتَيْنَٰهُ مِنَ ٱلْكُنُوزِ مَآ إِنَّ مَفَاتِحَهُۥ لَتَنُوٓأُ بِٱلْعُصْبَةِ أُو۟لِى ٱلْقُوَّةِ إِذْ قَالَ لَهُۥ قَوْمُهُۥ لَا تَفْرَحْ ۖ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ ٱلْفَرِحِينَ
record.translation: Indeed, Qarun was from the people of Moses, but he tyrannized them. And We gave him of treasures whose keys would burden a band of strong men; thereupon his people said to him, "Do not exult. Indeed, Allah does not like the exultant.
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: ثُمَّ بَعَثْنَا مِنۢ بَعْدِهِم مُّوسَىٰ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَآ إِلَىٰ فِرْعَوْنَ وَمَلَإِي۟هِۦ فَظَلَمُوا۟ بِهَا ۖ فَٱنظُرْ كَيْفَ كَانَ عَٰقِبَةُ ٱلْمُفْسِدِينَ
record.translation: Then We sent after them Moses with Our signs to Pharaoh and his establishment, but they were unjust toward them. So see how was the end of the corrupters.
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: وَٱذْكُرْ فِى ٱلْكِتَٰبِ مُوسَىٰٓ ۚ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ مُخْلَصًۭا وَكَانَ رَسُولًۭا نَّبِيًّۭا
record.translation: And mention in the Book, Moses. Indeed, he was chosen, and he was a messenger and a prophet.
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: ٱصْبِرْ عَلَىٰ مَا يَقُولُونَ وَٱذْكُرْ عَبْدَنَا دَاوُۥدَ ذَا ٱلْأَيْدِ ۖ إِنَّهُۥٓ أَوَّابٌ
record.translation: Be patient over what they say and remember Our servant, David, the possessor of strength; indeed, he was one who repeatedly turned back [to Allah].
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: وَٱلسَّلَٰمُ عَلَىَّ يَوْمَ وُلِدتُّ وَيَوْمَ أَمُوتُ وَيَوْمَ أُبْعَثُ حَيًّۭا
record.translation: And peace is on me the day I was born and the day I will die and the day I am raised alive."
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: وَيُكَلِّمُ ٱلنَّاسَ فِى ٱلْمَهْدِ وَكَهْلًۭا وَمِنَ ٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ
record.translation: He will speak to the people in the cradle and in maturity and will be of the righteous."
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: ٱلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ ٱلَّذِى وَهَبَ لِى عَلَى ٱلْكِبَرِ إِسْمَٰعِيلَ وَإِسْحَٰقَ ۚ إِنَّ رَبِّى لَسَمِيعُ ٱلدُّعَآءِ
record.translation: Praise to Allah, who has granted to me in old age Ishmael and Isaac. Indeed, my Lord is the Hearer of supplication.
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: ۞ وَإِذِ ٱبْتَلَىٰٓ إِبْرَٰهِۦمَ رَبُّهُۥ بِكَلِمَٰتٍۢ فَأَتَمَّهُنَّ ۖ قَالَ إِنِّى جَاعِلُكَ لِلنَّاسِ إِمَامًۭا ۖ قَالَ وَمِن ذُرِّيَّتِى ۖ قَالَ لَا يَنَالُ عَهْدِى ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
record.translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when Abraham was tried by his Lord with commands and he fulfilled them. [Allah] said, "Indeed, I will make you a leader for the people." [Abraham] said, "And of my descendants?" [Allah] said, "My covenant does not include the wrongdoers."
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: وَلَمَّا بَلَغَ أَشُدَّهُۥ وَٱسْتَوَىٰٓ ءَاتَيْنَٰهُ حُكْمًۭا وَعِلْمًۭا ۚ وَكَذَٰلِكَ نَجْزِى ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ
record.translation: And when he attained his full strength and was [mentally] mature, We bestowed upon him judgement and knowledge. And thus do We reward the doers of good.
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: ۞ وَلَقَدْ ءَاتَيْنَا دَاوُۥدَ مِنَّا فَضْلًۭا ۖ يَٰجِبَالُ أَوِّبِى مَعَهُۥ وَٱلطَّيْرَ ۖ وَأَلَنَّا لَهُ ٱلْحَدِيدَ
record.translation: And We certainly gave David from Us bounty. [We said], "O mountains, repeat [Our] praises with him, and the birds [as well]." And We made pliable for him iron,
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: وَقَٰتِلُوا۟ فِى سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلَّذِينَ يُقَٰتِلُونَكُمْ وَلَا تَعْتَدُوٓا۟ ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ ٱلْمُعْتَدِينَ
record.translation: Fight in the way of Allah those who fight you but do not transgress. Indeed. Allah does not like transgressors.
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: مِنْ أَجْلِ ذَٰلِكَ كَتَبْنَا عَلَىٰ بَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ أَنَّهُۥ مَن قَتَلَ نَفْسًۢا بِغَيْرِ نَفْسٍ أَوْ فَسَادٍۢ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ فَكَأَنَّمَا قَتَلَ ٱلنَّاسَ جَمِيعًۭا وَمَنْ أَحْيَاهَا فَكَأَنَّمَآ أَحْيَا ٱلنَّاسَ جَمِيعًۭا ۚ وَلَقَدْ جَآءَتْهُمْ رُسُلُنَا بِٱلْبَيِّنَٰتِ ثُمَّ إِنَّ كَثِيرًۭا مِّنْهُم بَعْدَ ذَٰلِكَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ لَمُسْرِفُونَ
record.translation: Because of that, We decreed upon the Children of Israel that whoever kills a soul unless for a soul or for corruption [done] in the land - it is as if he had slain mankind entirely. And whoever saves one - it is as if he had saved mankind entirely. And our messengers had certainly come to them with clear proofs. Then indeed many of them, [even] after that, throughout the land, were transgressors.
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ عَٰهَدتُّم مِّنَ ٱلْمُشْرِكِينَ ثُمَّ لَمْ يَنقُصُوكُمْ شَيْـًۭٔا وَلَمْ يُظَٰهِرُوا۟ عَلَيْكُمْ أَحَدًۭا فَأَتِمُّوٓا۟ إِلَيْهِمْ عَهْدَهُمْ إِلَىٰ مُدَّتِهِمْ ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُحِبُّ ٱلْمُتَّقِينَ
record.translation: Excepted are those with whom you made a treaty among the polytheists and then they have not been deficient toward you in anything or supported anyone against you; so complete for them their treaty until their term [has ended]. Indeed, Allah loves the righteous [who fear Him].
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: فَإِذَا ٱنسَلَخَ ٱلْأَشْهُرُ ٱلْحُرُمُ فَٱقْتُلُوا۟ ٱلْمُشْرِكِينَ حَيْثُ وَجَدتُّمُوهُمْ وَخُذُوهُمْ وَٱحْصُرُوهُمْ وَٱقْعُدُوا۟ لَهُمْ كُلَّ مَرْصَدٍۢ ۚ فَإِن تَابُوا۟ وَأَقَامُوا۟ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَءَاتَوُا۟ ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ فَخَلُّوا۟ سَبِيلَهُمْ ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورٌۭ رَّحِيمٌۭ
record.translation: And when the sacred months have passed, then kill the polytheists wherever you find them and capture them and besiege them and sit in wait for them at every place of ambush. But if they should repent, establish prayer, and give zakah, let them [go] on their way. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: وَإِنْ أَحَدٌۭ مِّنَ ٱلْمُشْرِكِينَ ٱسْتَجَارَكَ فَأَجِرْهُ حَتَّىٰ يَسْمَعَ كَلَٰمَ ٱللَّهِ ثُمَّ أَبْلِغْهُ مَأْمَنَهُۥ ۚ ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ قَوْمٌۭ لَّا يَعْلَمُونَ
record.translation: And if any one of the polytheists seeks your protection, then grant him protection so that he may hear the words of Allah. Then deliver him to his place of safety. That is because they are a people who do not know.
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: وَيَسْـَٔلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلرُّوحِ ۖ قُلِ ٱلرُّوحُ مِنْ أَمْرِ رَبِّى وَمَآ أُوتِيتُم مِّنَ ٱلْعِلْمِ إِلَّا قَلِيلًۭا
record.translation: And they ask you, [O Muhammad], about the soul. Say, "The soul is of the affair of my Lord. And mankind have not been given of knowledge except a little."
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: ٱللَّهُ يَتَوَفَّى ٱلْأَنفُسَ حِينَ مَوْتِهَا وَٱلَّتِى لَمْ تَمُتْ فِى مَنَامِهَا ۖ فَيُمْسِكُ ٱلَّتِى قَضَىٰ عَلَيْهَا ٱلْمَوْتَ وَيُرْسِلُ ٱلْأُخْرَىٰٓ إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلٍۢ مُّسَمًّى ۚ إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَءَايَٰتٍۢ لِّقَوْمٍۢ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ
record.translation: Allah takes the souls at the time of their death, and those that do not die [He takes] during their sleep. Then He keeps those for which He has decreed death and releases the others for a specified term. Indeed in that are signs for a people who give thought.
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: وَنَفْسٍۢ وَمَا سَوَّىٰهَا
record.translation: And [by] the soul and He who proportioned it
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: أَفَلَا يَتَدَبَّرُونَ ٱلْقُرْءَانَ ۚ وَلَوْ كَانَ مِنْ عِندِ غَيْرِ ٱللَّهِ لَوَجَدُوا۟ فِيهِ ٱخْتِلَٰفًۭا كَثِيرًۭا
record.translation: Then do they not reflect upon the Qur'an? If it had been from [any] other than Allah, they would have found within it much contradiction.
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: وَٱلسَّمَآءَ بَنَيْنَٰهَا بِأَيْي۟دٍۢ وَإِنَّا لَمُوسِعُونَ
record.translation: And the heaven We constructed with strength, and indeed, We are [its] expander.
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: هُوَ ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَ لَكُم مَّا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ جَمِيعًۭا ثُمَّ ٱسْتَوَىٰٓ إِلَى ٱلسَّمَآءِ فَسَوَّىٰهُنَّ سَبْعَ سَمَٰوَٰتٍۢ ۚ وَهُوَ بِكُلِّ شَىْءٍ عَلِيمٌۭ
record.translation: It is He who created for you all of that which is on the earth. Then He directed Himself to the heaven, [His being above all creation], and made them seven heavens, and He is Knowing of all things.
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: ثُمَّ ٱسْتَوَىٰٓ إِلَى ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَهِىَ دُخَانٌۭ فَقَالَ لَهَا وَلِلْأَرْضِ ٱئْتِيَا طَوْعًا أَوْ كَرْهًۭا قَالَتَآ أَتَيْنَا طَآئِعِينَ
record.translation: Then He directed Himself to the heaven while it was smoke and said to it and to the earth, "Come [into being], willingly or by compulsion." They said, "We have come willingly."
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: فَقَضَىٰهُنَّ سَبْعَ سَمَٰوَاتٍۢ فِى يَوْمَيْنِ وَأَوْحَىٰ فِى كُلِّ سَمَآءٍ أَمْرَهَا ۚ وَزَيَّنَّا ٱلسَّمَآءَ ٱلدُّنْيَا بِمَصَٰبِيحَ وَحِفْظًۭا ۚ ذَٰلِكَ تَقْدِيرُ ٱلْعَزِيزِ ٱلْعَلِيمِ
record.translation: And He completed them as seven heavens within two days and inspired in each heaven its command. And We adorned the nearest heaven with lamps and as protection. That is the determination of the Exalted in Might, the Knowing.
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: ءَأَنتُمْ أَشَدُّ خَلْقًا أَمِ ٱلسَّمَآءُ ۚ بَنَىٰهَا
record.translation: Are you a more difficult creation or is the heaven? Allah constructed it.
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: رَفَعَ سَمْكَهَا فَسَوَّىٰهَا
record.translation: He raised its ceiling and proportioned it.
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا بَلَغَ مَغْرِبَ ٱلشَّمْسِ وَجَدَهَا تَغْرُبُ فِى عَيْنٍ حَمِئَةٍۢ وَوَجَدَ عِندَهَا قَوْمًۭا ۗ قُلْنَا يَٰذَا ٱلْقَرْنَيْنِ إِمَّآ أَن تُعَذِّبَ وَإِمَّآ أَن تَتَّخِذَ فِيهِمْ حُسْنًۭا
record.translation: Until, when he reached the setting of the sun, he found it [as if] setting in a spring of dark mud, and he found near it a people. Allah said, "O Dhul-Qarnayn, either you punish [them] or else adopt among them [a way of] goodness."
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: وَلَقَدْ زَيَّنَّا ٱلسَّمَآءَ ٱلدُّنْيَا بِمَصَٰبِيحَ وَجَعَلْنَٰهَا رُجُومًۭا لِّلشَّيَٰطِينِ ۖ وَأَعْتَدْنَا لَهُمْ عَذَابَ ٱلسَّعِيرِ
record.translation: And We have certainly beautified the nearest heaven with stars and have made [from] them what is thrown at the devils and have prepared for them the punishment of the Blaze.
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: إِنَّا زَيَّنَّا ٱلسَّمَآءَ ٱلدُّنْيَا بِزِينَةٍ ٱلْكَوَاكِبِ
record.translation: Indeed, We have adorned the nearest heaven with an adornment of stars
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: وَإِذْ قَالَ ٱللَّهُ يَٰعِيسَى ٱبْنَ مَرْيَمَ ءَأَنتَ قُلْتَ لِلنَّاسِ ٱتَّخِذُونِى وَأُمِّىَ إِلَٰهَيْنِ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ ۖ قَالَ سُبْحَٰنَكَ مَا يَكُونُ لِىٓ أَنْ أَقُولَ مَا لَيْسَ لِى بِحَقٍّ ۚ إِن كُنتُ قُلْتُهُۥ فَقَدْ عَلِمْتَهُۥ ۚ تَعْلَمُ مَا فِى نَفْسِى وَلَآ أَعْلَمُ مَا فِى نَفْسِكَ ۚ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ عَلَّٰمُ ٱلْغُيُوبِ
record.translation: And [beware the Day] when Allah will say, "O Jesus, Son of Mary, did you say to the people, 'Take me and my mother as deities besides Allah?'" He will say, "Exalted are You! It was not for me to say that to which I have no right. If I had said it, You would have known it. You know what is within myself, and I do not know what is within Yourself. Indeed, it is You who is Knower of the unseen.
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: وَيُعَلِّمُهُ ٱلْكِتَٰبَ وَٱلْحِكْمَةَ وَٱلتَّوْرَىٰةَ وَٱلْإِنجِيلَ
record.translation: And He will teach him writing and wisdom and the Torah and the Gospel
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: وَرَسُولًا إِلَىٰ بَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ أَنِّى قَدْ جِئْتُكُم بِـَٔايَةٍۢ مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ ۖ أَنِّىٓ أَخْلُقُ لَكُم مِّنَ ٱلطِّينِ كَهَيْـَٔةِ ٱلطَّيْرِ فَأَنفُخُ فِيهِ فَيَكُونُ طَيْرًۢا بِإِذْنِ ٱللَّهِ ۖ وَأُبْرِئُ ٱلْأَكْمَهَ وَٱلْأَبْرَصَ وَأُحْىِ ٱلْمَوْتَىٰ بِإِذْنِ ٱللَّهِ ۖ وَأُنَبِّئُكُم بِمَا تَأْكُلُونَ وَمَا تَدَّخِرُونَ فِى بُيُوتِكُمْ ۚ إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَءَايَةًۭ لَّكُمْ إِن كُنتُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ
record.translation: And [make him] a messenger to the Children of Israel, [who will say], 'Indeed I have come to you with a sign from your Lord in that I design for you from clay [that which is] like the form of a bird, then I breathe into it and it becomes a bird by permission of Allah. And I cure the blind and the leper, and I give life to the dead - by permission of Allah. And I inform you of what you eat and what you store in your houses. Indeed in that is a sign for you, if you are believers.
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ قُلْ هُوَ ٱللَّهُ أَحَدٌ
record.translation: Say, "He is Allah, [who is] One,
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: ٱللَّهُ ٱلصَّمَدُ
record.translation: Allah, the Eternal Refuge.
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: وَلَمْ يَكُن لَّهُۥ كُفُوًا أَحَدٌۢ
record.translation: Nor is there to Him any equivalent."
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: مَا ٱتَّخَذَ ٱللَّهُ مِن وَلَدٍۢ وَمَا كَانَ مَعَهُۥ مِنْ إِلَٰهٍ ۚ إِذًۭا لَّذَهَبَ كُلُّ إِلَٰهٍۭ بِمَا خَلَقَ وَلَعَلَا بَعْضُهُمْ عَلَىٰ بَعْضٍۢ ۚ سُبْحَٰنَ ٱللَّهِ عَمَّا يَصِفُونَ
record.translation: Allah has not taken any son, nor has there ever been with Him any deity. [If there had been], then each deity would have taken what it created, and some of them would have sought to overcome others. Exalted is Allah above what they describe [concerning Him].
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: إِنَّ فِى خَلْقِ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ وَٱخْتِلَٰفِ ٱلَّيْلِ وَٱلنَّهَارِ لَءَايَٰتٍۢ لِّأُو۟لِى ٱلْأَلْبَٰبِ
record.translation: Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth and the alternation of the night and the day are signs for those of understanding.
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: ثُمَّ خَلَقْنَا ٱلنُّطْفَةَ عَلَقَةًۭ فَخَلَقْنَا ٱلْعَلَقَةَ مُضْغَةًۭ فَخَلَقْنَا ٱلْمُضْغَةَ عِظَٰمًۭا فَكَسَوْنَا ٱلْعِظَٰمَ لَحْمًۭا ثُمَّ أَنشَأْنَٰهُ خَلْقًا ءَاخَرَ ۚ فَتَبَارَكَ ٱللَّهُ أَحْسَنُ ٱلْخَٰلِقِينَ
record.translation: Then We made the sperm-drop into a clinging clot, and We made the clot into a lump [of flesh], and We made [from] the lump, bones, and We covered the bones with flesh; then We developed him into another creation. So blessed is Allah, the best of creators.
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: ٱلَّذِىٓ أَحْسَنَ كُلَّ شَىْءٍ خَلَقَهُۥ ۖ وَبَدَأَ خَلْقَ ٱلْإِنسَٰنِ مِن طِينٍۢ
record.translation: Who perfected everything which He created and began the creation of man from clay.
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِى جَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلْأَرْضَ قَرَارًۭا وَٱلسَّمَآءَ بِنَآءًۭ وَصَوَّرَكُمْ فَأَحْسَنَ صُوَرَكُمْ وَرَزَقَكُم مِّنَ ٱلطَّيِّبَٰتِ ۚ ذَٰلِكُمُ ٱللَّهُ رَبُّكُمْ ۖ فَتَبَارَكَ ٱللَّهُ رَبُّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
record.translation: It is Allah who made for you the earth a place of settlement and the sky a ceiling and formed you and perfected your forms and provided you with good things. That is Allah, your Lord; then blessed is Allah, Lord of the worlds.
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: ٱلَّذِى لَهُۥ مُلْكُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ وَلَمْ يَتَّخِذْ وَلَدًۭا وَلَمْ يَكُن لَّهُۥ شَرِيكٌۭ فِى ٱلْمُلْكِ وَخَلَقَ كُلَّ شَىْءٍۢ فَقَدَّرَهُۥ تَقْدِيرًۭا
record.translation: He to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and who has not taken a son and has not had a partner in dominion and has created each thing and determined it with [precise] determination.
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: أُذِنَ لِلَّذِينَ يُقَٰتَلُونَ بِأَنَّهُمْ ظُلِمُوا۟ ۚ وَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ نَصْرِهِمْ لَقَدِيرٌ
record.translation: Permission [to fight] has been given to those who are being fought, because they were wronged. And indeed, Allah is competent to give them victory.
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: ٱلَّذِينَ أُخْرِجُوا۟ مِن دِيَٰرِهِم بِغَيْرِ حَقٍّ إِلَّآ أَن يَقُولُوا۟ رَبُّنَا ٱللَّهُ ۗ وَلَوْلَا دَفْعُ ٱللَّهِ ٱلنَّاسَ بَعْضَهُم بِبَعْضٍۢ لَّهُدِّمَتْ صَوَٰمِعُ وَبِيَعٌۭ وَصَلَوَٰتٌۭ وَمَسَٰجِدُ يُذْكَرُ فِيهَا ٱسْمُ ٱللَّهِ كَثِيرًۭا ۗ وَلَيَنصُرَنَّ ٱللَّهُ مَن يَنصُرُهُۥٓ ۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَقَوِىٌّ عَزِيزٌ
record.translation: [They are] those who have been evicted from their homes without right - only because they say, "Our Lord is Allah." And were it not that Allah checks the people, some by means of others, there would have been demolished monasteries, churches, synagogues, and mosques in which the name of Allah is much mentioned. And Allah will surely support those who support Him. Indeed, Allah is Powerful and Exalted in Might.
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ يَسْـَٔلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلْأَنفَالِ ۖ قُلِ ٱلْأَنفَالُ لِلَّهِ وَٱلرَّسُولِ ۖ فَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَأَصْلِحُوا۟ ذَاتَ بَيْنِكُمْ ۖ وَأَطِيعُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥٓ إِن كُنتُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ
record.translation: They ask you, [O Muhammad], about the bounties [of war]. Say, "The [decision concerning] bounties is for Allah and the Messenger." So fear Allah and amend that which is between you and obey Allah and His Messenger, if you should be believers.
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: إِنَّمَا ٱلْمُؤْمِنُونَ ٱلَّذِينَ إِذَا ذُكِرَ ٱللَّهُ وَجِلَتْ قُلُوبُهُمْ وَإِذَا تُلِيَتْ عَلَيْهِمْ ءَايَٰتُهُۥ زَادَتْهُمْ إِيمَٰنًۭا وَعَلَىٰ رَبِّهِمْ يَتَوَكَّلُونَ
record.translation: The believers are only those who, when Allah is mentioned, their hearts become fearful, and when His verses are recited to them, it increases them in faith; and upon their Lord they rely -
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: ٱلَّذِينَ يُقِيمُونَ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَمِمَّا رَزَقْنَٰهُمْ يُنفِقُونَ
record.translation: The ones who establish prayer, and from what We have provided them, they spend.
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْمُؤْمِنُونَ حَقًّۭا ۚ لَّهُمْ دَرَجَٰتٌ عِندَ رَبِّهِمْ وَمَغْفِرَةٌۭ وَرِزْقٌۭ كَرِيمٌۭ
record.translation: Those are the believers, truly. For them are degrees [of high position] with their Lord and forgiveness and noble provision.
record.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

record.arabic: وَأَعِدُّوا۟ لَهُم مَّا ٱسْتَطَعْتُم مِّن قُوَّةٍۢ وَمِن رِّبَاطِ ٱلْخَيْلِ تُرْهِبُونَ بِهِۦ عَدُوَّ ٱللَّهِ وَعَدُوَّكُمْ وَءَاخَرِينَ مِن دُونِهِمْ لَا تَعْلَمُونَهُمُ ٱللَّهُ يَعْلَمُهُمْ ۚ وَمَا تُنفِقُوا۟ مِن شَىْءٍۢ فِى سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ يُوَفَّ إِلَيْكُمْ وَأَنتُمْ لَا تُظْلَمُونَ
